drugs.mechanism: Antibody preferentially binding soluble aggregated Aβ, particularly protofibrils, and promoting amyloid clearance.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for AD; accelerated approval January 2023 and traditional approval July 2023.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials targeting aggregated Aβ in early symptomatic AD supported approval.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody recognizing N-terminal pyroglutamate-modified Aβ enriched in plaques and promoting plaque clearance.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials targeting plaque-associated Aβ in early symptomatic AD supported approval.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding aggregated Aβ, including oligomeric and fibrillar species.
drugs.fdaStatus: Historical FDA accelerated approval for AD in June 2021; commercialization and development subsequently discontinued.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials targeting aggregated Aβ in early AD; clinical results were inconsistent.

drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug of tramiprosate intended to inhibit toxic Aβ oligomer formation; the Aβ interaction is mediated by its active drug.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not FDA-approved for AD according to the supplied review.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Evaluated through Phase 3 for prevention of Aβ oligomer formation in early AD.

drugs.mechanism: Aβ-interacting small molecule intended to inhibit oligomer formation; active drug delivered by valiltramiprosate.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 AD trials evaluated its Aβ-directed anti-aggregation approach without establishing efficacy in the overall trial population.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody preferentially binding soluble monomeric Aβ.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 treatment and prevention trials targeting soluble Aβ did not establish clinical benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody recognizing aggregated Aβ and promoting amyloid removal.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials targeting aggregated Aβ in early AD did not establish clinical benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Investigational translational regulator intended to reduce APP and other neurodegeneration-associated proteins; direct binding to APP protein is not established.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinical trials in AD have evaluated the protein-production-lowering strategy, including Phase 2/3 studies; these do not establish direct APP-protein binding.

drugs.mechanism: Target APP RNA to reduce APP expression rather than bind APP protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: No FDA-approved APP-directed AD treatment identified.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No specific agent or clinical-trial phase is identified in the supplied text; direct APP-protein binding is not the intended mechanism.

drugs.mechanism: BACE1 inhibition reduces amyloidogenic APP cleavage and Aβ production.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials for BACE1 inhibition in AD were stopped for lack of benefit and concerns including cognitive worsening.

drugs.mechanism: BACE1 inhibition reduces Aβ production.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2/3 and Phase 3 AD trials of BACE1 inhibition were terminated for futility.

drugs.mechanism: BACE1 inhibition reduces amyloidogenic APP processing.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinical development, including a Phase 2b/3 prevention study, tested BACE1 inhibition; the program was stopped amid liver toxicity and cognitive safety concerns.

drugs.mechanism: BACE1 inhibition reduces Aβ production.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials of BACE1 inhibition in early AD were terminated because of an unfavorable benefit-risk assessment.

drugs.mechanism: BACE1 inhibition reduces amyloidogenic APP processing.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2/3 prevention trials of BACE1 inhibition were stopped following cognitive worsening and other safety concerns.

drugs.mechanism: Broad γ-secretase inhibition; effects on presenilin-containing complexes do not establish PSEN1 or PSEN2 selectivity.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials of γ-secretase inhibition in AD were stopped because of worsening outcomes and toxicity.

drugs.mechanism: γ-Secretase inhibitor developed to favor inhibition of APP processing over Notch processing; not established as presenilin-isoform selective.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trials of γ-secretase inhibition in AD did not establish a favorable benefit-risk profile.

drugs.mechanism: Investigated as a γ-secretase modulator intended to alter Aβ product distribution; direct complex binding and adequate brain target engagement were not established by the review.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 AD trial of the proposed γ-secretase-modulating strategy failed to demonstrate efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Phosphodiesterase-4D inhibitor, not a γ-secretase modulator; no direct interaction with a requested protein is established.
drugs.fdaStatus: Investigational; no FDA approval identified in the supplied review.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; clinical investigation concerns PDE4D inhibition rather than the listed proteins.

drugs.mechanism: Investigational γ-secretase modulator intended to shift APP cleavage toward shorter Aβ peptides rather than broadly inhibit proteolysis.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No clinical-trial phase for this specific compound is established by the supplied text.

drugs.mechanism: γ-Secretase inhibitor; oncology use does not establish suitability for chronic AD treatment or presenilin-isoform selectivity.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for adults with progressing desmoid tumors requiring systemic treatment; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 trials tested γ-secretase inhibition in desmoid tumors and supported approval; no established AD efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Retinoid-dependent transcriptional regulation can increase ADAM10/α-secretase expression; not an established direct α-secretase ligand.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for severe psoriasis; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: A small randomized AD clinical study evaluated indirect enhancement of nonamyloidogenic APP processing; it did not establish direct α-secretase binding.

drugs.mechanism: Protein kinase C modulator investigated for synaptic effects and nonamyloidogenic APP processing; not a selective α-secretase ligand.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 AD trials evaluated PKC-mediated effects, not direct binding to a listed protein.

drugs.mechanism: Antisense oligonucleotide targeting MAPT RNA to reduce tau production; does not directly bind tau protein.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 1b and Phase 2 AD studies evaluate MAPT transcript reduction and tau lowering, not direct MAPT-protein binding.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding tau epitopes, intended to affect extracellular tau pathology and propagation.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trials targeting tau in AD have not established consistent clinical benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Anti-tau antibody intended to limit extracellular tau-mediated pathology.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trial targeting tau in early AD did not demonstrate clinical benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Anti-tau antibody intended to reduce extracellular tau propagation.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trial targeting tau in early AD did not establish efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody recognizing a tau epitope and intended to limit pathological tau propagation.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Evaluated in a Phase 2 trial targeting tau in early AD; clinical benefit is not established by the supplied review.

drugs.mechanism: Proposed tau aggregation inhibition; the intended protein interaction should not be treated as proof of clinical efficacy.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 3 AD trials have evaluated tau aggregation inhibition; efficacy remains unestablished in the supplied review.

drugs.mechanism: Indirect tau-pathway modulation through mechanisms including GSK3 inhibition; not a selective tau ligand.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for bipolar disorder; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Small clinical trials in AD or mild cognitive impairment have evaluated indirect disease-modifying effects, including tau-related biomarkers; no established direct MAPT-targeting trial.

drugs.mechanism: Agonist antibody intended to enhance membrane TREM2 signaling; activity against sTREM2 should not be inferred from this description.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trial of TREM2 agonism in early AD did not demonstrate clinical efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Supplies soluble TREM2 ectodomain activity; sTREM2 is the administered therapeutic protein, not an established binding target of itself.
drugs.fdaStatus: No FDA-approved sTREM2 treatment for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Predominantly preclinical in the supplied review; no clinical trial of a specified recombinant sTREM2 product is identified.

drugs.mechanism: Prodrug whose active metabolite R406 inhibits SYK downstream of TYROBP-associated signaling; not a TYROBP-binding drug.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for chronic immune thrombocytopenia; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; established clinical use concerns SYK inhibition rather than direct TYROBP targeting.

drugs.mechanism: Active metabolite of fostamatinib that inhibits SYK; downstream modulation does not establish TYROBP binding.
drugs.fdaStatus: Active metabolite of FDA-approved fostamatinib; not separately identified as an approved AD drug.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets.

drugs.mechanism: Reversible, predominantly acetylcholinesterase-selective inhibition increases cholinergic neurotransmission.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Multiple randomized clinical trials of ACHE inhibition in AD supported approval.

drugs.mechanism: Reversible competitive acetylcholinesterase inhibition; not an equipotent ACHE/BCHE inhibitor at therapeutic exposure.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Randomized clinical trials of ACHE inhibition in AD supported approval.

drugs.mechanism: Carbamate-mediated inhibition of acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Randomized AD trials evaluated dual cholinesterase inhibition and supported approval; individual contributions of ACHE and BCHE inhibition were not necessarily isolated.

drugs.mechanism: Prodrug converted to galantamine; ACHE inhibition is mediated by the active drug rather than established direct binding by benzgalantamine.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in 2024 for mild-to-moderate dementia of the Alzheimer’s type.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Approval relies on delivery of galantamine and its established ACHE-directed clinical evidence, with supporting pharmacokinetic studies rather than a separate demonstration of direct prodrug binding.

drugs.mechanism: Inhibits both acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase; use was limited by hepatotoxicity.
drugs.fdaStatus: Historical FDA-approved AD treatment; no longer routinely marketed or used.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinical trials of cholinesterase inhibition in AD supported historical approval.

drugs.mechanism: Investigational selective butyrylcholinesterase inhibitor.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No clinical-trial phase or completed target-specific trial is established in the supplied text.

drugs.mechanism: Low-to-moderate-affinity, voltage-dependent, uncompetitive open-channel NMDA receptor blocker.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Randomized trials of NMDA receptor blockade in moderate-to-severe AD supported approval.

drugs.mechanism: Combines memantine-mediated NMDA receptor channel blockade with donepezil-mediated ACHE inhibition.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved fixed-dose symptomatic treatment for moderate-to-severe AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinical studies evaluated combined NMDA receptor blockade and ACHE inhibition in AD; the fixed-dose product also relies on component efficacy and pharmacokinetic bridging.

drugs.mechanism: NMDA-related antagonist pharmacology, substantially mediated by its metabolite dextrorphan; not an established AD cognitive treatment.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved in antitussive products and certain combination products for other indications; not approved as an AD cognitive treatment.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Dextromethorphan-containing combinations have been studied for AD-associated agitation; these studies do not isolate NMDA receptor-specific efficacy.

drugs.mechanism: Has NMDA receptor antagonist activity among its pharmacological actions; shared pharmacology with memantine does not establish AD efficacy.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for non-AD indications, including parkinsonism; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No target-specific AD clinical trial is established in the supplied text.

drugs.mechanism: RXR agonist investigated for indirect enhancement of APOE-related lipid transport pathways; does not directly target APOE protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: A small AD clinical trial evaluated the RXR/APOE-pathway hypothesis; direct APOE binding and clinical benefit were not established.

drugs.mechanism: APOE2 gene-delivery therapy intended to alter CNS APOE isoform biology; not a drug that binds existing APOE protein.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 1/2 clinical investigation of APOE2 gene delivery in APOE ε4 homozygotes with AD; this is isoform supplementation, not direct protein binding.

drugs.mechanism: Target APOE RNA to reduce expression rather than bind APOE protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: No FDA-approved APOE-directed AD treatment identified.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Described as preclinical in the supplied text; no named clinical agent or trial is identified.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody binding α-synuclein, encoded by SNCA; developed primarily for synucleinopathies.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not FDA-approved according to the supplied review.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 clinical trials targeting α-synuclein in Parkinson’s disease; not an established AD treatment.

drugs.mechanism: Anti-α-synuclein antibody developed for synucleinopathies.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Phase 2 trial targeting α-synuclein in Parkinson’s disease did not establish efficacy; not an established AD treatment.

drugs.mechanism: Mucolytic investigated as a glucocerebrosidase chaperone; effects on α-synuclein handling are indirect, not validated α-synuclein binding.
drugs.fdaStatus: Not FDA-approved; used as a mucolytic in some countries.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Clinical studies in Parkinson’s disease and related conditions evaluate glucocerebrosidase enhancement, not direct binding to a listed protein.

drugs.mechanism: ALS drug with glutamatergic and other neuronal effects; not established as a direct TDP-43/TARDBP therapy or a direct binder of a requested protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for ALS; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No established clinical trials specifically targeting TARDBP through direct riluzole binding; AD investigation does not establish that mechanism.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody directly blocking the inhibitory immune receptor PD-1; AD repurposing is an experimental immune-clearance hypothesis.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for multiple oncology indications; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensive clinical trials, including Phase 3, establish PD-1 blockade in cancer; no clinically established AD benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Antibody directly blocking PD-1; proposed AD effects are experimental and accompanied by substantial immune-mediated toxicity risks.
drugs.fdaStatus: FDA-approved for multiple oncology indications; not approved for AD.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: Extensive clinical trials, including Phase 3, establish PD-1 blockade in cancer; no clinically established AD benefit.

drugs.mechanism: Multicomponent herbal preparation; network pharmacology does not establish a validated interaction with any requested protein.
drugs.fdaStatus: No FDA approval established in the supplied text.
drugs.trialStatusForTargets: No known trials for these targets; the supplied text provides no target-specific clinical evidence.
